title: Bounded construction of an appended record
statement: For every nonnegative integer $m$, there are a finite state set $P$, distinctness decidable on $P$, a two-work-tape machine $R$, entry and exit states, and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ with the following property. Let $h$ be a header word, let $es$ be a list of lists of words, and let $e$ be a list of words of length $m$, with every word in the table formed by $h$ followed by the flattened entries of $es$ nonempty. If a configuration $d$ starts in the entry state, tape 0 has head position $o$ and contains that table in its joined-field encoding, tape 0 is blank at every position at or beyond the table's end, and tape 1 contains the joined-field encoding of $e$ at its head, then for some time $t\le C(L+E+1)$, where $L$ and $E$ are the lengths of those two joined encodings, running $R$ for $t$ steps reaches the exit state and leaves every work-tape head within distance $C(L+E+1)$ of its starting position. The exit is not reached earlier; at time $t$, tape 0 contains the encoding of $e$ beginning at the table offset after all its fields, with the tape head at that offset, while every other tape cell agrees with its initial content.
